input.title: fix: give Phasing its own active behavior clock
input.body:
## Summary

```text
Phasing clip constructor → integer counter 0–50
  → register first behavior ID (preserve all visual parts)
  → active World part update after movement
       counter ≤ 50: fade out
       150 < counter ≤ 200: fade in
       counter = 300: reset counter, retain alpha
```

Recover the Phasing portion of original `928a5c6`. Replace the actor-age/UID formula with a private behavior counter. Jam, stun and pause suspend it; boss movement does not bypass it. World/rebuild/wave/spawn factories supply the shared RNG context.

Reuse the already-probed signed 8.8 display-alpha setter, correcting the old checkpoint's decimal accumulator. Preserve the existing duration-plus-reset status encoding and release boundary. Movement and other behavior controllers remain separate follow-up slices.

## Evidence

- **Before:** A jammed actor advances its old age-derived fade to alpha 0.94 instead of holding alpha 1; the regression fails.
  **After:** Seven focused cases cover suspension/release, partial first fade, complete windows/reset residue, registration with unchanged visual records, independent integer constructor counters and boss behavior.
- Source/pcode confirms the counter windows and constructor, clip construction before duplicate registration, and movement→jam→parts ordering. From counter 0/alpha 1, the clock retains alpha 136/256 at frame 20, −1/256 at 50/150, and 249/256 at 200/reset 300.
- Formatting, TypeScript, 605 tests / 6,766 assertions and production build pass. Eight distinct affected native/mock browser cases pass across runs: final focused paint pair (6.9s), fresh-game pilot pair, and existing artwork/protection cases. Negative model alpha paints transparent; fixed-pose galleries match after reset. Both captures inspected.
- Pilots reach boss/win/continue using the existing upgrade-selection adapter; this is narrower than an original-runtime playthrough comparison. Full constructor/Setup RNG interleaving, remaining movement/target/behavior state and Adobe/game parity remain unfinished. No generated metadata or original media added.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** Two-way

No persisted schema migration; revert clock state, factory context and part-update wiring together.

**Blast Radius:** Simulation

Phasing alpha and behavior registration now follow their own active lifecycle. New constructor draws intentionally use the shared World RNG; full source-wide RNG ordering remains unfinished.
